summary: The appeal challenged the High Court's order upholding the Commercial Court's refusal to grant additional time to the appellant to file a written statement, which was barred after 120 days from service of summons under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC as amended by the Commercial Courts Act, 2015. Key issues included whether the limitation extension due to COVID-19 (under Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No. 3 of 2020) applied to procedural deadlines like filing written statements. The Court held that extension orders did not cover procedural time limits, and the Trial Court correctly declined further extension beyond 120 days, despite pandemic-related difficulties. Technical non-compliance resulted in forfeiture of the right to file a written statement.
legal_provisions_cited: Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Section 12-A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015
Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No. 3 of 2020
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed. The orders of the Commercial Court and High Court were upheld. The appellant forfeited its right to file a written statement due to non-compliance with the 120-day limit under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC.
